findings.title: The anti-vacuity docblock names a trigger that does not fire: dropping `as const` from AUTO_APPROVAL_BLOCK_PRECEDENCE produces neither the claimed vacuity nor the claimed TS2578
findings.arbiter_reasoning: Measured three ways. M5: `as const` removed, `satisfies readonly AutoApprovalBlockReason[]` kept -> tsc --noEmit reports ZERO diagnostics, so the promised TS2578 does not appear. M5b: the same edit plus a dropped rank -> TS2344 still fires at vocabulary.ts:650 and vocabulary.test.ts:697 naming "rating_below_threshold", so _Whole is NOT vacuous under that edit and Ranks[number] does not swallow the union - the satisfies contextual type preserves the element literals. M5c: the real widening, `export const AUTO_APPROVAL_BLOCK_PRECEDENCE: readonly AutoApprovalBlockReason[] = [...]` -> TS2578 fires at vocabulary.test.ts:706 exactly as described. The guard is genuine and load-bearing; the comment misidentifies which edit triggers it and asserts a hazard the named edit does not create. Graded P1 not P0 because no shipped guarantee is misrepresented: the assertion works and the guard fires on the real hazard. Behavioural replacement: name the annotated form, or say 'any widening that erases the element literal types'.

findings.title: The property test's false-green arithmetic is wrong by roughly 5x, and the same figure is repeated in the plan and the intake
findings.arbiter_reasoning: The comment claims a 22-member pool would witness a hole 'roughly 0.4% per run, ~86% over 500 runs. A 14% false green'. 0.4% is the independent-coin model (1/2 * 1/2^7 = 1/256), which is not how fc.shuffledSubarray samples. Measured against fast-check@4.9.0 from this lockfile: the subset LENGTH histogram over 100000 draws from a 22-member pool is roughly uniform (lengths 1-5 at ~7.1% each, 6-22 at ~3.8% each, mean 10.05), not binomial; the per-run witness rate is 4049/200000 = 2.02%; and detection over 500 runs across 4000 independent trials is 1.0000, i.e. a false-green rate near 0%, not 14%. The design decision the paragraph justifies (pool = the map's non-null keys) remains correct and strictly better, so this is a false justification rather than a wrong test - P1, not P0. The same numbers appear at plan:245 and in .feature/intake.json edge_cases[9], so a later reader has three chances to inherit them.

findings.arbiter_reasoning: The docblock says the map is read through its OWN `as const satisfies` type and that widening it makes every key survive `extends null` and resolve to the full 22. Measured: M4 (drop `as const`, keep `satisfies`) -> zero diagnostics, values keep their RefusalCategory literals through the contextual type; M4b (same plus a dropped rank) -> TS2344 still names the member, so the derivation is intact; M4c (the real widening, an explicit Record<...> annotation) -> TS2344 naming "policy_not_enabled" on a HEALTHY tree plus TS2322 at the lookup. Same class as RT1080-01 but lower stakes because the conclusion is right.
